records.prompt:
Given
\[
f(x)=|\sin x|,\qquad -\pi\le x\le\pi,
\]
and
\[
g(x)=x^2
\]
for all real values of \(x\).

partsPatches.label: (a)
partsPatches.answer: On \([-\pi,0]\), \(\sin x\le0\), so \(f(x)=-\sin x\). On \([0,\pi]\), \(f(x)=\sin x\). Thus the graph consists of two nonnegative sine arches, with included zeros at \(x=-\pi,0,\pi\) and maxima \(1\) at \(x=\pm\frac{\pi}{2}\).

rubric.description: 1 point for reflecting the negative sine arch above the \(x\)-axis.
rubric.evidenceRequired: 1 point for reflecting the negative sine arch above the \(x\)-axis.

rubric.description: 1 point for the correct key points and included endpoints at \(x=\pm\pi\).
rubric.evidenceRequired: 1 point for the correct key points and included endpoints at \(x=\pm\pi\).

partsPatches.label: (c)
partsPatches.answer:
The composition uses the same allowed inputs as \(f\), because \(g\) is defined for every real input. Hence
\[
\operatorname{Dom}(H)=\boxed{[-\pi,\pi]}.
\]
Since \(0\leq\sin^2x\leq1\), and both values are attained,
\[
\operatorname{Range}(H)=\boxed{[0,1]}.
\]

partsPatches.label: (a)
partsPatches.answer:
If \(k=0\), both tangent lines are horizontal, so no such perpendicular pair exists. For \(k\ne0\), since \(f'(x)=2kx\), the two slopes at \(x_0\) and \(-x_0\) are \(2kx_0\) and \(-2kx_0\). Their product must be \(-1\):
\[
(2kx_0)(-2kx_0)=-1.
\]
Thus \(4k^2x_0^2=1\). One convenient choice is
\[
\boxed{x_0=\frac1{2k}},
\]
and the opposite choice merely interchanges the two tangent points.

records.prompt:
The function \(f\) is defined for every real number by
\[
f(x)=2|x-1|x^2.
\]

partsPatches.label: (a)
partsPatches.answer:
Because \(2|x-1|x^2\ge0\), and it equals \(0\) at \(x=0\) and \(x=1\), the minimum value is \(0\). Also \(f(x)\to\infty\) as \(x\to\pm\infty\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Range}(f)=[0,\infty)}.
\]

rubric.description: 1 point for identifying that \(0\) is attained at \(x=0\) and \(x=1\).
rubric.evidenceRequired: 1 point for identifying that \(0\) is attained at \(x=0\) and \(x=1\).

partsPatches.label: (c)
partsPatches.answer:
Write the function piecewise:
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}2x^2-2x^3,&x<1,\\2x^3-2x^2,&x\ge1.\end{cases}
\]
Thus
\[
f'(x)=\begin{cases}4x-6x^2,&x<1,\\6x^2-4x,&x>1.\end{cases}
\]
At \(x=1\), the one-sided derivatives are \(-2\) and \(2\), so \(f'\) does not exist there. Hence \(f'\) is continuous on
\[
\boxed{(-\infty,1)\cup(1,\infty)}.
\]

rubric.description: 1 point for the correct integrand and antiderivative.
rubric.evidenceRequired: 1 point for the correct integrand and antiderivative.
